source.title: Current safety training techniques do not fully transfer to the agent setting

record.tranche_reason: This is a post summarizing and discussing other papers. It reports no independent test or application of the claim's direction or interventions.
record.gate_note: The post summarizes results attributed to AgentHarm, BrowserART, and the refusal-vector ablation paper. The reported refusal rates and ablation findings are results from other work, not results of this post, so they are not entered as rows.
record.test_reason: The post summarizes three other papers (AgentHarm, BrowserART, the refusal-vector ablation agents paper). The refusal-vector ablation result on Llama 3.1 agents comes from arXiv:2410.10871, which the author co-wrote, and is cited rather than produced here. The post itself runs no new experiment on the direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author argues that chat-model safety training does not fully transfer to agents, while attacks (jailbreaks, prompt rewriting, refusal-vector ablation) do transfer. He reads this as evidence that capabilities generalize further than alignment.
record.recipe_differences: No method is independently applied or compared in this post.
record.problems: The post is a secondary summary and explicitly notes that the three papers' results are not directly comparable. Its reported results are attributed to those papers rather than independently tested here.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Numerical refusal rates and ablation outcomes are summaries of cited papers and are excluded under the rule against recording results cited from other work.

untested.parts: No new ablation or addition of the direction, and no capability check.
No weight edit performed. The ablated-Llama agent result is cited from arXiv:2410.10871.
No test of jailbreaks suppressing the direction, and no adversarial training against its ablation.
Mentions a chat-derived vector working in the agent setting, but cited only. No language, variant or base-to-instruct test.
Not addressed. o1-preview appears only in cited refusal rates, with no direction test.

record.verdict_notes: The cited ablation result is relevant to V2/V6, but its source is arXiv:2410.10871, which should be recorded as its own study: ablation removes all refusals in agent tasks, using a vector computed on chat requests. Comments (e.g., Martin Randall's reading of Table 2) also restate that paper's numbers; these are not new results.

versions.untested_parts: No independent test of finding, ablating, or adding a difference-in-means direction, or of effects on general capability.
No weight edit or independent test of released-model abliteration.
The post summarizes another paper's refusal-vector ablation result, but does not test attacks that suppress the direction or training against its ablation.
No test or argument comparing a single direction with an affine, cone, or multi-direction account.
No test of whether harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from refusal.
The post discusses transfer from chat models to agents, but does not test transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
No test of how refusal training or its timing affects the existence of a removable direction.
No test of the claim in reasoning models.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
